notes:
**SCCM Retro - Update 2.26.0**

Your CPU clock is yours again. You pick it, and nothing changes it behind your back.

**Overclocking and tuning**
- **CPU Settings** replaces the old CPU Clock page. Pick your max clock and your max voltage, and that is what the console runs. The voltage limit that used to choose your clock for you is gone: it could not reach the range people were setting it to, and enforcing it was quietly undoing your power profile's CPU cap.
- **A new CPU voltage ceiling**, enforced by the chip itself rather than watched and reacted to. 1120 mV on V2 and OLED, 1225 mV on V1. Needs the kernel update included in this release.
- Pick a clock your chip cannot actually reach and the console measures that when you apply, then saves the fastest it really delivers. Asking for more than that only raises voltage for nothing.
- **A table of what each clock really costs on your chip**, average and peak, gathered while you play. It sits next to the clock picker so you can choose with real numbers instead of a spec sheet.
- **GPU Settings** gains a switch for the 1075 MHz GPU cap. That cap has been on your console all along with no way to see or change it. It stays on by default.
- **Stock CPU undervolt presets** are selectable again, and picking one now genuinely replaces the tuned undervolt instead of losing to it. Six levels, or off.
- A console with no clock saved starts somewhere sensible for its model: 1963 MHz without an undervolt and 2397 MHz with one on V2 and OLED, 1785 and 2091 on V1. Your existing clock is kept exactly as it is.

**Bug fixes**
- **Battery Saver and the other power profiles keep their CPU cap.** They were being silently lifted back to your full overclock, which is why switching profiles and switching back looked like it fixed things.
- **Battery power draw reads correctly.** Small values were multiplied by a thousand, so a console sipping 0.02 W could show 23 W. Docked consoles saw this most.
- **Settings pages with a single row respond to the D-pad again.** The CPU voltage limit could only be changed by touchscreen until you touched it once.
- Applying a CPU voltage change now offers to restart, instead of telling you a restart is needed and leaving you to find one.

Known issues
- No V1 console has run any of this. Every V1 number here comes from reading the code, not from a console. Reports welcome.
- The new voltage ceiling will not change anything on most consoles today. It sits above where a healthy chip already runs, and only bites when the chip is cold, poorly binned, or its undervolt has been backed off.
- Turning the GPU cap off is untested. Nobody has measured what a console does above 1075 MHz. Watch temperatures and power draw if you try it.

Released OTA
